artifact: Scientific Relation, Conflict and Gap Registry

relations.interpretation: Multi-domain assessment and active acquisition of missing information are complementary process claims.
AHA BP guidance defines BP/risk management context, whereas USPSTF counseling has its own eligibility population.
General dietary guidance is broader than individualized assessment/reference construction.
BMI-based eligibility for a specific obesity behavioral recommendation is narrower than generic nutrition/weight considerations.

conflict_summary: No direct scientific contradiction requiring adjudication was identified in the initial six-source set. Scope differences and temporal-update status are preserved as relations/uncertainties rather than manufactured conflicts.

gaps.description: Current authorized case view lacks direct dietary intake/pattern information; day-1 total energy is explicitly UNKNOWN because the source component has not been ingested.
gaps.impact: Blocks confident individualized diet-specific recommendation and leaves nutrition-assessment sufficiency unresolved.

gaps.description: Current case view does not expose a complete medical/risk context needed to determine applicability of risk-conditioned cardiovascular counseling or management recommendations.
No qualified source in the current set defines a universal minimal variable checklist that must always be present before any individualized nutrition recommendation.
gaps.impact: Prevents conversion of the KnowledgeNeed contract into a rigid mandatory checklist.

gaps.description: No qualified source in the current set establishes DEFER as the uniquely correct action for EP-NHANES-L-0001.
gaps.impact: Final action remains a reference-construction question rather than a D1 scientific fact.

gaps.description: USPSTF counseling/weight-loss topics are flagged as being updated at the evidence cutoff.
Live-web sources are not byte-frozen and the 2025 AHA/ACC guideline correction lineage has not been reconstructed claim-by-claim.
gaps.impact: Blocks final D1-G6 ScientificReferenceState reproducibility PASS.
